urbanRural.classification: ONS 2021 Rural Urban Classification of Local Authority Districts (2024)
urbanRural.referencePeriod: Census 2021 populations; council boundaries of 2024 (published 9 March 2025)
urbanRural.method: A council's class reflects where most of its population lives: urban (20 % or less in rural Output Areas), intermediate urban (more than 20 % to 35 %), intermediate rural (more than 35 % to 50 %) or majority rural (more than 50 %), split by whether most of the population is nearer to or further from a major town or city. It describes settlement form, not landscape or economy.

notCovered.Scotland: The Scottish Government Urban Rural Classification is published for Data Zones, not councils; it is not yet included.
notCovered.Northern Ireland: NISRA publishes no council-level urban/rural class. Its 2015 settlement-based class is shown for small areas in the neighbourhood analysis where available.

carAvailability.measure: Households with no car or van available, of all households

notCovered.Scotland: Scotland's census was held in 2022; its car or van availability tables are not yet included.

carAvailability.comparability: England and Wales (ONS) and Northern Ireland (NISRA) asked about cars or vans available to household members on the same census day, 21 March 2021. Scotland's census was a year later and is not included.
